definitions.explanation: A large body of water surrounded by land. Bigger than a pond ({池|いけ}).

examples.english: We camped with our family at a quiet lake in the mountains.

notes:
{湖|みずうみ} refers to a lake - a large body of water surrounded by land.

ETYMOLOGY:
The native word みずうみ is みず (water) + うみ (sea): a "freshwater sea." The kanji {湖|みずうみ} is a single character, not a spelling of those two.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {湖|みずうみ}: lake (large)
- ⟦{池|いけ}→池：00848_ike⟧: pond (small)
- ⟦{沼|ぬま}→沼：02160_numa⟧: marsh, swamp

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {湖|みずうみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{畔|ほとり}→畔：27482_hotori⟧: lakeside
- {湖|みずうみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一周|いっしゅう}→一周：08917_isshuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to go around the lake
- {湖|みずうみ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{釣|つ}り→釣り：03439_tsuri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to fish in a lake

RELATED WORDS (lakes in Japan):
- ⟦{琵琶湖|びわこ}→琵琶湖：29592_biwako⟧: Lake Biwa (largest in Japan)
- {河口湖|かわぐちこ}: Lake Kawaguchi (near Mt. Fuji)
- {十和田湖|とわだこ}: Lake Towada

USAGE:
Lake names use the Sino-Japanese reading ～{湖|こ} as a suffix: ⟦{琵琶|びわ}{湖|こ}→琵琶湖：29592_biwako⟧, {河口|かわぐち}{湖|こ}.
